_: Six of the eight are behaviour the previous build did not have: it had no
resolve_git at all, and its check C could not reach git on this machine,
so it refused on every run. Those fail against the reconstructed build.
Assertions 06 and 07 are the two that matter most and the two a version
control CANNOT prove. They say NO_SECRETS still exits non-zero and says
so when git cannot be reached at all -- and the previous build did that
too, because it could never reach git. An assertion that agrees with both
branches is not evidence, and this is exactly the assertion an over-eager
So they are controlled by mutation `weaken`, which drops tracked_err from
the blocking test -- the precise weakening the owner asked to be guarded
against. Under it, a run that cannot reach git exits 0 and reads as a
clean publish; both assertions catch it.

assertions.name: 01 git is resolved on this machine without being on PATH
02 check C reads the index instead of refusing
03 NO_SECRETS_GIT naming a missing file refuses, and does not fall back
04 a named git that exists but will not run is refused too
05 with git genuinely absent the resolver finds nothing and says why
06 NO_SECRETS still refuses, loudly, when git cannot be reached

mutation.why: drop tracked_err from the blocking test, so a check that could not run exits 0, and see both refusal assertions catch it
mutation.find:
blocked = bool(path_hits or secret_hits or tracked_hits or tracked_err
                   or binary_hits)
mutation.replace:
blocked = bool(path_hits or secret_hits or tracked_hits
                   or binary_hits)

assertions.name: 07 a working git that cannot answer also blocks
08 against the real tree check C runs and the tree passes
